note: The hard cases. Each has a genuine federal component this corpus covers AND a component it does not. A flat decline is wrong; a confident complete answer is worse. Expected behaviour is labelled per question.

categories.PARTIAL: Answer the federal part from the corpus AND flag what it cannot decide.
categories.DECLINE: Sounds wage-and-hour but is governed elsewhere. Decline and route.
categories.FULL: Entirely answerable from the corpus. Control, to detect over-declining.

questions.q: I am a salaried manager in California earning $70,000. Am I owed overtime?
questions.why: Federal exemption test is in the corpus; California sets its own higher salary threshold and stricter duties test.

questions.q: My employer pays me every two weeks. Is that legal?
questions.why: Pay frequency is state law. The FLSA does not set it.

questions.q: Am I owed double time for working a Sunday?
questions.why: Federal law requires no premium for weekends as such; some states do.

questions.q: My employer did not give me my final paycheck when I quit. What can I do?
I am 16 and work 30 hours a week during school. Is that allowed?
questions.why: Child labour is 29 CFR 570, which is not in this corpus, though it sounds squarely wage-and-hour.

questions.q: Can my employer make me work twelve-hour shifts?
questions.why: Federal law caps no hours for adults, only requires overtime past 40; state daily-overtime rules differ.

questions.q: I was misclassified as a contractor. Can I sue for back overtime?
questions.why: Classification test is in the corpus; the right to sue, damages and limitation periods are not.

questions.q: Can my employer cut my hours so I lose my health benefits?
questions.why: Benefits eligibility is ERISA and the ACA, not wage-and-hour.

questions.q: My tips were pooled with the kitchen staff. Is that legal?
Do I get paid for a fifteen minute coffee break?
My employer requires unpaid training on Saturdays. Is that legal?
I am an undocumented worker. Am I still owed the minimum wage?
questions.why: The corpus defines wage obligations without reference to status; immigration consequences are elsewhere.
